thread.title: DSG passes resolution to support reaffiliating of greek-life
thread.title_full: DSG passes resolution to support reaffiliating of greek-life

author: Jeremiah Fang
title: DSG passes resolution to support reaffiliating of greek-life
text:
DSG senators passed a resolution supporting the reaffiliation of greek-life, discussed turning duARTs into an DSG affiliate and heard from Mary Pat McMahon, vice provost and vice president of student affairs during its Wednesday meeting.
Reaffiliation of greek-life
Senators passed a resolution saying the DSG executive board will "pursue efforts to support reaffiliation of these organizations,” which include fraternities, sororities and Durham Interfraternity Council.
“This is an effort to bring them back, bring social life back onto campus, and promote campus safety in general,” said junior Yash Sharma, vice president of Durham and community affairs.
Nine fraternities disaffiliated in 2021 following changes to the rush process in preparation for the QuadEx residential system, introduced in fall 2021. After disaffiliating from Duke’s Interfraternity Council, the nine fraternities then joined the then-newly formed Durham Interfraternity Council (IFC) and continued operations as off-campus organizations.
The resolution also formally recognizes a committee advisory board composed of greek-life leadership dedicated to “getting feedback” and ensuring that student affairs and other leaders will “be on the same page.”
The resolution was established with the intention of fostering a safer, more inclusive environment for students both on and off campus.
Partnership with Student Affairs
Mary Pat McMahon, vice provost and vice president of student affairs, emphasized the connection between student affairs and DSG. McMahon identified previous partnerships, such as the free laundry initiative, as examples of DSG’s work with student affairs.
In her address, McMahon gave advice to senators to both strengthen DSG's partnership with academic affairs and help ensure that senators are able to more effectively utilize their time in leadership roles.
“I could give you 25 years of examples of people that I worked with in the seat that you're in right now who then figured out a way to do something and then they went on to lead in so many different ways,” McMahon said.
In other business
duARTS, an umbrella organization for student art groups on campus, presented a resolution to become an affiliate of DSG.
duARTS, currently a SOFC funded organization, would have more direct access to DSG funding as an affiliate, and can improve representation of arts groups on campus.
Voting to officially turn duARTS into a DSG affiliate will take place at the next senate meeting.
Members for the committee on financial oversight were selected. This includes juniors Edison Chen and Samanyu Gangappa, sophomores Clark Easley and Ryan Jankelowitz and first-years Shrihaan Chaudhary, Asher Schenk and Jonathan Fromm.
